Approximate Procedure-Level False Positive Rate

Source: R/fpr_approximation.R
fpr_approx.Rd

Computes an analytical approximation to the ForestSearch false positive rate under the null hypothesis of homogeneous treatment effect. The calculation accounts for (i) the sampling variability of the effect estimate in a subgroup of size n_min, (ii) the number of candidate subgroups searched (driven by the covariate space and maxk), and (iii) the screening threshold c1.

Usage

fpr_approx(
  effect_true = 0.65,
  p_event = 0.4,
  n_min = 60L,
  c1 = 1.25,
  n_confounders_cont = 6L,
  n_confounders_bin = 6L,
  cont_cutoff = 4L,
  maxk = 2L,
  effect_type = c("ratio", "difference"),
  treat_alloc = 0.5,
  rho = 0.3,
  n_eff = NULL,
  thresholds = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

effect_true

Numeric. True effect under H0 on the ratio scale (e.g., OR or HR). Default 0.65 (protective treatment).

p_event

Numeric in (0, 1). Overall event rate (control arm baseline rate for binary; used to compute SE). Default 0.40.

n_min

Integer. Minimum subgroup size (n.min in forestsearch()). Default 60.

c1

Numeric. The screening threshold on a candidate subgroup's own effect – forestsearch's effect.threshold (legacy hr.threshold). Candidates with effect > c1 pass screening. Default 1.25. This approximation covers the screening stage only, so the per-split effect threshold c2 (consistency.threshold) and the consistency rate p* (pconsistency.threshold) do not appear here.

n_confounders_cont

Integer. Number of continuous confounders. Default 6.

n_confounders_bin

Integer. Number of binary confounders. Default 6.

cont_cutoff

Integer. Number of cut points per continuous covariate (cont.cutoff in forestsearch()). Each continuous variable produces cont_cutoff candidate subgroups. Default 4.

maxk

Integer. Maximum interaction depth. 1 = single-variable subgroups only; 2 = up to two-variable interactions. Default 2.

effect_type

Character. "ratio" (OR, HR, IRR: log-scale SE) or "difference" (RD, MD: identity-scale SE). Default "ratio".

treat_alloc

Numeric in (0, 1). Treatment allocation fraction. Default 0.5 (1:1 randomisation).

rho

Numeric in [0, 1). Assumed average pairwise correlation between candidate test statistics, used for the correlation-adjusted FPR estimate. Default 0.30. Set to 0 for the independence (upper-bound) estimate only. Ignored when n_eff is set.

n_eff

Numeric or NULL. Pre-specified effective number of independent tests. When set, overrides the rho-based Sidak adjustment. Default NULL (compute from rho).

thresholds

Numeric vector. Additional thresholds to evaluate besides c1. Default c(1.0, 1.5, 2.0).

verbose

Logical. Print a formatted summary. Default TRUE.

Value

A list (class "fpr_approximation") with components:

se_log_effect

SE of log(effect) in a subgroup of size n_min.

n_candidates

Total number of candidate subgroups searched.

n_single

Number of single-variable candidates.

n_pairs

Number of two-variable candidates (0 if maxk == 1).

per_candidate

Named numeric vector: P(effect > thr) for each threshold evaluated.

fpr_indep

Named numeric vector: procedure-level FPR assuming independent candidates, for each threshold.

fpr_adjusted

Named numeric vector: correlation-adjusted FPR, for each threshold.

params

List of input parameters.

Details

The approximation assumes:

  • Normal approximation to the log-OR (or log-HR) distribution.

  • Independent candidates (upper bound; true FPR is lower due to overlap). A correlation-adjusted estimate is also returned.

  • Equal allocation to treatment arms within each subgroup.

  • No consistency check adjustment (the reported FPR is the screening-stage FPR before pconsistency.threshold filtering).

Examples

# ACTG175 binary harm search
fpr_approx(effect_true = 0.65, p_event = 0.40, n_min = 60, c1 = 1.25)
#> ============================================================
#>   ForestSearch FPR Approximation (screening stage)
#> ============================================================
#> 
#>   True effect (H0):   0.650  (log = -0.431)
#>   Event rate (ctrl):  40.0%
#>   Event rate (trt):   30.2%  (implied by OR = 0.65)
#>   Min subgroup (n):   60  (~30 per arm)
#>   SE(log effect):     0.545
#> 
#>   Confounders:        6 continuous (x4 cuts) + 6 binary
#>   Single candidates:  30
#>   Pair candidates:    435  (maxk = 2)
#>   Total candidates:   465
#>   Effective tests:    3  (rho = 0.30)
#> 
#>   Threshold   P(per candidate)   FPR (indep)   FPR (adj)
#>   ---------   ----------------   -----------   ---------
#>     1.25         11.5%             100.0%         33.3% <-- c1
#> 
#>   Note: Screening-stage only.  Consistency check (pconsistency)
#>   and bootstrap correction further reduce the operational FPR.
#>   Independence FPR is an upper bound; adjusted uses Sidak with
#>   effective tests (rho = 0.30).
#> ============================================================

# Tighter threshold
fpr_approx(effect_true = 0.65, p_event = 0.40, n_min = 60, c1 = 2.0)
#> ============================================================
#>   ForestSearch FPR Approximation (screening stage)
#> ============================================================
#> 
#>   True effect (H0):   0.650  (log = -0.431)
#>   Event rate (ctrl):  40.0%
#>   Event rate (trt):   30.2%  (implied by OR = 0.65)
#>   Min subgroup (n):   60  (~30 per arm)
#>   SE(log effect):     0.545
#> 
#>   Confounders:        6 continuous (x4 cuts) + 6 binary
#>   Single candidates:  30
#>   Pair candidates:    435  (maxk = 2)
#>   Total candidates:   465
#>   Effective tests:    3  (rho = 0.30)
#> 
#>   Threshold   P(per candidate)   FPR (indep)   FPR (adj)
#>   ---------   ----------------   -----------   ---------
#>     2.00          2.0%             100.0%          6.3% <-- c1
#> 
#>   Note: Screening-stage only.  Consistency check (pconsistency)
#>   and bootstrap correction further reduce the operational FPR.
#>   Independence FPR is an upper bound; adjusted uses Sidak with
#>   effective tests (rho = 0.30).
#> ============================================================

# Larger minimum subgroup
fpr_approx(effect_true = 0.65, p_event = 0.40, n_min = 100, c1 = 1.25)
#> ============================================================
#>   ForestSearch FPR Approximation (screening stage)
#> ============================================================
#> 
#>   True effect (H0):   0.650  (log = -0.431)
#>   Event rate (ctrl):  40.0%
#>   Event rate (trt):   30.2%  (implied by OR = 0.65)
#>   Min subgroup (n):   100  (~50 per arm)
#>   SE(log effect):     0.422
#> 
#>   Confounders:        6 continuous (x4 cuts) + 6 binary
#>   Single candidates:  30
#>   Pair candidates:    435  (maxk = 2)
#>   Total candidates:   465
#>   Effective tests:    3  (rho = 0.30)
#> 
#>   Threshold   P(per candidate)   FPR (indep)   FPR (adj)
#>   ---------   ----------------   -----------   ---------
#>     1.25          6.1%             100.0%         18.7% <-- c1
#> 
#>   Note: Screening-stage only.  Consistency check (pconsistency)
#>   and bootstrap correction further reduce the operational FPR.
#>   Independence FPR is an upper bound; adjusted uses Sidak with
#>   effective tests (rho = 0.30).
#> ============================================================
